FRBRname.value: Bundesgesetz vom 20. März 2009 über die Patentanwältinnen und Patentanwälte (Patentanwaltsgesetz, PAG)
Legge federale del 20 marzo 2009 sui consulenti in brevetti (Legge sui consulenti in brevetti, LCB)
Federal Act of 20 March 2009 on Patent Attorneys (Patent Attorney Act, PatAA)
Loi du 20 mars 2009 sur les conseils en brevets (LCBr)

preface.p: English is not an official language of the Swiss Confederation. This translation is provided for information purposes only and has no legal force.

preamble.p: The Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation,

on the basis of Article 95 of the Federal Constitution
SR 101,
and having considered the Federal Council Dispatch of 7 December 2007
BBl 2008 407,

section.heading: Subject Matter and Scope of Application

item.p: the requirements for the use of the professional titles “patent attorney”, “Patentanwältin” or “Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets” and “consulente in brevetti”;
professional confidentiality applicable to patent attorneys;
the protection of the professional titles “European patent attorney”, “europäische Patentanwältin” or “europäischer Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets européens” and “consulente in brevetti europei”.

content.p: It is applicable to persons who provide advice or representation in patent matters in Switzerland using any of the professional titles mentioned in paragraph 1 letter a or c.

The representation of parties in proceedings before the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) by natural and legal persons residing or having their principal place of business in the Principality of Liechtenstein is governed by Article 8 of the Patent Treaty of 22 December 1978
SR 0.232.149.514 between the Swiss Confederation and the Principality of Liechtenstein.

blockList.listIntroduction: Any person who uses the title “patent attorney”, “Patentanwältin” or “Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets” or “consulente in brevetti” must:

item.p: possess a recognised higher education qualification in natural sciences or engineering (Art. 4 and 5);
have passed the Swiss Federal Patent Attorney Examination or a recognised foreign patent attorney examination (Art. 6 and 7);
have completed practical training (Art. 9);
possess at least an address for service in Switzerland; and
be registered in the Patent Attorney Register (Art. 11 et seq.).

content.p: Any person who uses the title “European patent attorney”, “europäische Patentanwältin” or “europäischer Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets européens” or “consulente in brevetti europei” must be registered in the list of professional representatives maintained by the European Patent Office.

Natural sciences or engineering degrees (Bachelor’s, Master’s, Diplom or Lizenziat) issued by an accredited Swiss higher education institution are considered to be recognised Swiss higher education qualifications in terms of this Act.
The Federal Council shall regulate the accreditation of Swiss higher education institutions.

article.heading: Recognition of foreign higher education qualifications

blockList.listIntroduction: A foreign higher education qualification in natural sciences or engineering is recognised where its equivalence to a recognised Swiss higher education qualification:

item.p: is provided for in a treaty pertaining to mutual recognition with the respective state or supranational organisation; or
is proven in an individual case.

content.p: The Federal Council shall designate the competent bodies for such recognition. It shall designate a single body where possible.
Where the competent bodies do not recognise a foreign higher education qualification, they shall decide how the requirement of Article 2 letter a may be fulfilled.
The Swiss Federal Patent Attorney Examination serves as proof of the specialised knowledge required for professional qualification.

item.p: the admission requirements for the examination;
the content of the examination;
the examination procedure.
the body competent for conducting the examination;
the body competent for the supervision of the examination.

article.heading: Recognition of foreign patent attorney examinations

blockList.listIntroduction: A foreign patent attorney examination is recognised where its equivalence to the Swiss Federal Patent Attorney Examination:

item.p: is provided for in a treaty pertaining to mutual recognition with the respective state or supranational organisation; or
is proven in an individual case.

content.p: The Federal Council shall designate the competent body for such recognition.
Where the competent body does not recognise a foreign patent attorney examination, it shall decide how the requirements of Article 2 letter b may be fulfilled.

article.heading: Delegation of tasks to organisations and persons of public or private law

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may entrust organisations and persons of public or private law with:

item.p: conducting the Swiss Federal Patent Attorney Examination;
deciding on the recognition of foreign patent attorney examinations;
issuing rulings concerning the passing of the Swiss Federal Patent Examination or the recognition of a foreign patent attorney examination.

content.p: The organisations and persons mentioned in paragraph 1 may levy fees for the rulings and services rendered by them. Their fee regulations are subject to approval by the Federal Council.

An objection may be filed with the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation
Term in accordance with No I 31 of the Ordinance of 15 June 2012 (Reorganisation of the Departments), in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3655). to rulings issued by the organisations and persons mentioned in paragraph 1.

Practical training as defined in Article 2 letter c must be completed under the supervision of a registered patent attorney (Art. 11 et seq.) or a person with an equivalent professional qualification.

The duration of practical training must amount to three years on a full-time basis for persons with a higher education qualification (Master’s, Diplom or Lizenziat degree) or a recognised equivalent qualification, and four years on a full-time basis for persons with a Bachelor’s degree or a recognised equivalent qualification. At least one year of the practical training must be related to Switzerland.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall regulate the particulars, including:

item.p: the objectives and content of the practical training;
the requirements to be fulfilled by a supervisor who is not registered in the Patent Attorney Register;
the requirements with regard to how the practical training is related to Switzerland in terms of territory and content.

content.p: Patent attorneys are obliged to maintain confidentiality concerning all secrets that are entrusted to them in their professional capacity or which come to their knowledge in the course of their professional activities, this obligation being unlimited in time.
They must ensure that persons assisting them maintain professional confidentiality.
The IPI shall maintain the Patent Attorney Register. It may maintain the Register in electronic form.
On application and on payment of a fee, the IPI shall register persons who fulfil the requirements of Article 2 in the Patent Attorney Register. It shall issue a certificate of registration.
The person making the application must prove by way of suitable documentation that he or she fulfils the requirements of Article 2.
The Federal Council may authorise the IPI to regulate electronic communication in accordance with the general provisions on the administration of federal justice.
The dossier and files may be maintained and stored in electronic form.

blockList.listIntroduction: Where the professional conduct of a patent attorney gives rise to complaints, the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) may, after hearing the person concerned:

item.p: admonish him or her;
authorise the IPI to disqualify him or her temporarily or permanently from using the professional title.

content.p: In assessing professional conduct within the meaning of paragraph 1, the patent attorney’s entire business activities in Switzerland and abroad shall be taken into consideration.
The FDJP may order the publication of the admonition or the disqualification as well as the deletion of the registration from the Patent Attorney Register.

blockList.listIntroduction: When registering patent attorneys in the Patent Attorney Register, the IPI shall enter the following particulars:

item.p: date of registration;
surname, first name, date of birth and place of origin or citizenship;
address for service or business address in Switzerland; and
name of employer, if applicable.

content.p: Patent attorneys must notify the IPI immediately of any changes to their registered particulars so that they may be registered in the Patent Attorney Register.
Any person may view the Register and obtain information on its content.
The IPI may make the content of the Register available to third parties by way of electronic retrieval.

blockList.listIntroduction: A fine shall be imposed on any person who, in his or her business documents, advertising of any kind, or other documents intended for use in business in Switzerland:

item.p: uses the title “patent attorney”, “Patentanwältin” or “Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets” or “consulente in brevetti” without being registered in the Patent Attorney Register;

uses the title “European patent attorney”, “europäische Patentanwältin” or “europäischer Patentanwalt”, “conseil en brevets européens” or “consulente in brevetti europei” or a title that may be confused with any of these titles without being registered in the list of professional representatives maintained by the European Patent Office.

content.p:
The use of a professional title in accordance with Article 9 of the Liechtenstein Act of 9 December 1992
Liechtenstein Law Gazette 1993 No. 43 on Patent Attorneys for the representation of parties in proceedings before the IPI by natural and legal persons residing or having their principal place of business in the Principality of Liechtenstein is reserved.
The prosecution of criminal offences is the responsibility of the cantons.
The amendment of current legislation is regulated in the Annex.

blockList.listIntroduction: A person shall be registered in the Patent Attorney Register on application and on payment of a fee provided that, on commencement of this Act, he or she has been working professionally as a patent attorney on a full-time basis in Switzerland:

item.p: for more than six years, possesses a higher education qualification in natural sciences or engineering from a Swiss higher education institution or a foreign higher education qualification as defined in Article 5 paragraph 1, and has an address for service in Switzerland; or
for more than three years, is registered in the list of professional representatives maintained by the European Patent Office and has an address for service in Switzerland.

content.p: Application must be made within two years of commencement of this Act.
The applicant must prove, by means of suitable documentation, that he or she fulfils the requirements of paragraph 1 letter a or b.
The IPI shall issue a certificate of registration.
This Act is subject to an optional referendum.
The Federal Council shall determine the commencement date.

Commencement date: 1 July 2011
Federal Council Decree of 11 May 2011
